D201.call_notes:
Rep: Thanks for making time again, and for bringing Omar. Last week we got through payroll and time-off. Today I thought we'd go to benefits administration.
Casper Fairweather (Chief People Officer): Right. Let me frame it with numbers so we don't wander. We have 83 people across two states, 71 enrolled in medical, 58 in dental, 44 in vision, and we have four carriers. Omar touches every one of them every month.
Omar Okonkwo (Benefits Manager): Every single month. So, here is my question, and I asked it on the first call too. When someone changes their plan in your system, what happens next? Does the carrier get it?
Rep: The enrollment gets recorded in Lanternmere, and you'd get an export you can download and send, and we'd give you the template for each carrier.
Omar Okonkwo (Benefits Manager): Download and send. By hand.
Rep: By hand, yes. Not a live feed.
Omar Okonkwo (Benefits Manager): Okay. So that is, what, four files, sometimes six when someone has a qualifying event. I do that now in a spreadsheet. The whole reason we are looking is to stop doing that. I spent eleven hours on it in October. Eleven.
Casper Fairweather (Chief People Officer): And that is the part I can't get past. Everything else you showed us I liked. The payroll runs were clean, the tax filings looked fine, the dashboard is better than ours. But if Omar still sends files, then I have bought a nicer spreadsheet.
Rep: Could the export be scheduled?
Casper Fairweather (Chief People Officer): Scheduled by whom, though? Somebody still has to check it landed. A feed that goes straight to the carrier, with errors flagged, that is the requirement. Is that on the roadmap?
Rep: I can't give you a date I'd stand behind.
Casper Fairweather (Chief People Officer): Then that's honest, and I appreciate it. Look, the budget is tight this year too, I'll say that, we were going to be stretching for the first year regardless. But that isn't what's stopping us. Omar, anything to add?
Omar Okonkwo (Benefits Manager): Just the feeds. Everything hangs on the feeds.

D202.call_notes:
Rep: Ms. Vasquez, good to see you again. I want to begin by apologizing for how long it took us to get this demo on the calendar.
Hollis Vasquez (Chief People Officer): Thank you. I will be candid, if I may. Three weeks is a long interval. Twenty-one days, to be precise, since our first conversation.
Rep: It is, and that is on us. Scheduling slipped on our side.
Hollis Vasquez (Chief People Officer): I understand how these things happen. The difficulty is that when we spoke in the first week, our owner was keen. He asked me daily for an update. By the second week he had stopped asking, and by the third I had begun a conversation with Corvane, simply because they were able to meet with us promptly. I do not say that to be unkind.
Dariusz Cadogan (Controller): If I may add something. From the finance side, I had set aside a block of time in the middle of the month to review the proposal. That window has since closed. I am now closing the quarter, and I cannot give it the attention it deserves.
Rep: That is fair. Would it help if I walked through just the payroll and reporting pieces, in thirty minutes?
Dariusz Cadogan (Controller): It might have, a fortnight ago.
Hollis Vasquez (Chief People Officer): To be fair, what I have seen today is thoughtful. The onboarding flow is tidy. Dariusz, you were pleased with the journal export, were you not?
Dariusz Cadogan (Controller): I was. It is a good export.
Hollis Vasquez (Chief People Officer): But we are already partway through another evaluation, and there is a trial running with our IT manager's team. I do not wish to start again from the beginning. I would rather be straightforward with you than let this drift.
Rep: I appreciate that. I will send a short note afterward.
Hollis Vasquez (Chief People Officer): Please do. And thank you for your courtesy.
D202.closing_email:
Subject: Following up on today's demo

Hollis,

Thank you for your candor today. I am sorry the demo took three weeks to arrange; that was our delay, and I understand the momentum had moved on by then. If your other evaluation does not work out, or priorities change, I would be glad to pick this up again at short notice.

D203.call_notes:
Yuki Thorsen (HR Director): Sorry, I'm eating lunch at my desk, it's that kind of week. Go ahead, I'm listening.
Rep: No problem. Casper's joining too, right?
Yuki Thorsen (HR Director): He is. He's late because finance is always late. Anyway, I'll say it before he gets here. We're going with you.
Rep: That's great to hear.
Yuki Thorsen (HR Director): Honestly I was ready to pick whoever annoyed me least. I'm doing HR and half of operations for sixty-four people and I do not have the energy for a long evaluation. The Brasswick people sent me a deck and it was fine. Fine. But your demo was the first one where I asked a question and you didn't go to a slide. You pulled up my actual scenario, the part-timer who changes states mid-quarter. Nobody else did that.
Rep: Glad that landed.
Yuki Thorsen (HR Director): And then the plan for getting us live. You put dates on it. Who does what, what I have to hand over and when. I can sleep with that.
Casper Brannigan (VP Finance): Sorry, sorry, back to back calls. Did I miss the part where she tells you yes?
Yuki Thorsen (HR Director): You did.
Casper Brannigan (VP Finance): Fine. I still have questions. What does the implementation cost if we slip a week? And if payroll fails in the first month, who is on the hook, us or you?

Casper Brannigan (VP Finance): Okay. Okay, that's clearer than what I got from the other vendor. I was going to push back on the timeline, but honestly, I'm fine. Yuki, you were right.

D206.call_notes:
Casper Galbraith (Office Manager): Okay. Quick one. We're not moving forward. I'll tell you why.

Casper Galbraith (Office Manager): I get it. But I had a problem right then. Our payroll person quit. I was running payroll myself. I needed a fix in days, not a week and a half. So I called Brasswick Payroll. They had someone on a screen share the next morning.

Rep: Is there flexibility if we adjust the contract term or the modules?
Soren Thorsen (COO): I asked. Even at a three-year term we were at $33,000. The partners wanted twenty-five at the outside.
Marisol Eastwood (HR Director): One other thing, minor. We had hoped for applicant tracking, since we hire hygienists constantly. Brasswick doesn't have it fully either, so I can't say it counted against you.
Soren Thorsen (COO): It's a nice-to-have. We'd have lived without it. If your number were 27 or 28, we'd be having a different call.
Rep: I understand. Thanks for laying it out so clearly.
Soren Thorsen (COO): Of course.
